citeAs: Antol, S., Agrawal, A., Lu, J., Mitchell, M., Batra, D., Zitnick, C. L., and Parikh, D. (2015). VQA: Visual question answering. In The IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV).
creator: Stanislaw Antol, Aishwarya Agrawal, Jiasen Lu, Margaret Mitchell, Dhruv Batra, C. Lawrence Zitnick, Devi Parikh
description: The VQA Dataset consists of real images from the COCO dataset (COCO-VQA) and abstract cartoon images (SYNTH-VQA). COCO-VQA contains 614,163 QA pairs (248,349 training, 121,512 validation, 244,302 testing) with three questions per image and ten answers per question. It supports both open-ended and multiple-choice evaluation formats.
name: The VQA Dataset (COCO-VQA)
rai:annotationsPerItem: 10 answers per question (collected from 10 independent annotators)
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-human agreement on COCO-VQA using AccuracyVQA is 83.3%. Agreement is especially poor for 'Why' questions, with over 59% of these questions having less than three annotators giving exactly the same answer. More than 13% of yes/no questions have both 'yes' and 'no' repeated by more than three annotators. The consensus-based evaluation metric (AccuracyVQA = min(n/3, 1)) awards full score when an algorithm agrees with 3 or more of the 10 annotators.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: AMT workers were asked to generate questions designed to 'Stump a smart robot' for each image. A separate pool of workers generated answers to those questions. Each question received 10 independent answers. The multiple-choice format includes: the correct answer (most frequent answer from 10 annotators), 3 plausible answers (collected without seeing the image), 10 popular answers (top-10 most popular in dataset), and random correct answers from other questions.
rai:dataBiases: COCO-VQA has strong language biases: many questions can be accurately answered without using the image, with image-blind algorithms achieving 49.6% accuracy using the question alone. 'Yes/no' answers span about 38% of all questions, and almost 59% of them are answered with 'yes'. More than 13% of yes/no answers have both 'yes' and 'no' repeated by more than three annotators. The dataset contains many subjective, opinion-seeking questions without a single objective answer. Questions are phrased with strong biases toward certain answers, and VQA systems are sensitive to slight variations in question phrasing. Natural image datasets tend to have more consistent context and biases (e.g., a street scene is more likely to have a dog than a zebra).
rai:dataCollection: Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) workers were employed to generate questions for each image by being asked to 'Stump a smart robot,' and a separate pool of workers were hired to generate the answers to the questions. Each question was answered by 10 independent annotators.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images from the Microsoft Common Objects in Context (COCO) dataset (real images) and synthetic cartoon images. COCO consists of 328,000 images with 91 common object categories and over 2 million labeled instances. The synthetic portion (SYNTH-VQA) consists of 50,000 synthetic scenes made from over 100 different objects, 30 different animal models, and 20 human cartoon models.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, User-generated content data
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset contains many questions that can be answered without using the image due to language biases. It contains subjective, opinion-seeking questions that do not have a single objective answer. Inter-human agreement is only 83.3%, making 100% accuracy impossible. The evaluation metric (AccuracyVQA) can lead to inflated scores; for example, answering 'yes' to all yes/no questions yields 71% accuracy instead of the expected ~50%. Many questions seek explanations or verbose descriptions that are difficult to evaluate automatically. The dataset is not sufficiently large to reach performance asymptotes during training.
rai:dataSocialImpact: VQA systems enabled by this dataset could aid blind and visually impaired individuals by allowing them to query images on the web and in the real world. The dataset also supports research toward a Visual Turing Test, which would represent a milestone in artificial intelligence for image understanding.
rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluating Visual Question Answering (VQA) algorithms. Applications include: aiding blind and visually impaired individuals to get information about images, improving human-computer interaction as a natural way to query visual content, image retrieval without metadata or tags, and serving as a component of a Visual Turing Test for image understanding.
